subject: physics
question_text: How does fusion energy reproduce a natural process that happens in our universe?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 14 Very Short Answer Question 9 (printed p.143). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. Chapter 14 is new to the 2026-27 syllabus and no board has examined it, so there is no exam history to cite. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: stellar fusion joins light nuclei, mainly hydrogen, into helium, and the small loss of mass appears as energy, which is the process fusion energy research reproduces.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The process
lines: that powers the Sun and the other
steps.why: Fusion research aims to reproduce, on Earth, the same reaction that has released energy inside stars for billions of years.
common_mistakes: Naming only the Sun without saying stars in general.
steps.memory_tip: Fusion copies the Sun and the stars, not a machine already on Earth.
steps.margin_note: The word Sun or star must appear in this step.

steps.label: What happens

lines.text: Light nuclei join to form helium.

lines: The small loss of mass appears as
steps.why: The mass of the helium formed is slightly less than the mass of the hydrogen nuclei that joined; that missing mass appears as the released energy.
common_mistakes: Writing that mass is destroyed instead of saying it appears as energy.
Naming a heavier element than helium as the product.
steps.memory_tip: Hydrogen joins to form helium; the missing mass becomes energy.
steps.margin_note: Hydrogen joining to form helium is the reaction to name here.
